recipes.name: Tequila Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds large shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Saute garlic until light brown. Place shrimp in the pan, and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in tequila, and season with cilantro, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tequila Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Jumbo shrimp sauteed in garlic, cilantro, and tequila Great over pasta, or enjoy with cocktail sauce.

review.reviewBody: What an excellent meal we made with this! We marinated 2lbs of shrimp in 1/2 cup tequila, 1/2 cup beer, some cilantro, garlic, and lime juice for about a 1/2 hour before sautéing with a tbsp of butter and some chopped onions. We served with black beans, pepper jack cheese, chopped tomatoes and avocados in whole wheat tortillas. You really can't make a more healthy or delicious meal!

After reading the reviews, I too modified this dish for my wife and I. A little Cilantro goes a long way, so I reduced it a lot. I used these ingredients: 2 tbs each butter and olive oil, 1/2 yellow onion-chopped, 4 cloves garlic, 1/2 tsp pepper flakes, 1 tbs cilantro, 14oz 61/40 shrimp, 1/4 cup each - Lite beer & white tequila, juice of 1 lime. Melt butter and oil at med heat, add onion till not quite translucent, add garlic, pepper flakes & cilantro - 2 min, add shrimp - 3 min, add tequila/beer mixture - 1 min. We only had angel hair pasta to eat it over - trust me, it works. We will definitely make this again. Enjoy

This was so easy and turned out great! I did make a few changes though. I followed the advice in the reviews and only used half of the tequila that the recipe calls for. I substituted Corona for the other half. I also added the juice of one lime and marinated the shrimp in this mixture for about an hour. I cooked the shrimp and garlic in the butter and then added the marinade with cilantro, salt, pepper, and a good helping of chili powder for the last two minutes of cooking. Wow, it was off the hook! We ate it over garlic buttered pasta and my husband licked the plate :) This recipe is also good because it gives you an excuse to buy tequila. And beer. We'll definitely do this recipe again the next time we want shrimp!

This was fantastic! I made some changes. I used 1/4 cup tequila and 1/4 cup lime juice and put them in with the garlic before the shrimp. When the shrimp was cooked, I mixed 1 tsp cornstarch and 2 tbsp water and added it to thicken up the sauce. I put them in flour tortillas and YUM! They were even awesome as cold leftovers the next day.

I also followed some of the reviews and added beer. It was great. also changed to:use 1/2 c. tequila, 1/2 c. light beer, 4 cloves garlic, onion, cilantro, juice of 2 - 3 limes, crushed red pepper and marinate for 30 minutes. Saute w/ 1 bag frozen roasted corn. serve w/whole wheat tortillas, beans and rice and cheese

This was awesome but, I have to admit the other reviewers talked me into some changes. First, I squeezed a full lime into a glass measuring cup, added enough tequila to make a full cup, added a splash of contreau to that and then added maybe 1 tablespoon of cilantro (all left that hadn't died in my garden), 3 green onions, 4 minced garlic cloves & I let it all marinate with the shrimp (and some sea scallops too) for 20 minutes or so. The scallops were a nice addition but not needed. I just like them so I often add them to recipes calling for shrimp.
I served it over angel hair pasta and it was very nice.

I pretty much didn't follow this recipe at all, however I did use it as inspiration. I cooked about two ounces of chorizo in a pan then sauteed two cloves of garlic and about half of a large yellow onion with it. I then cooked the shrimp in with this mixture and added in 1/4 C tequila and 1/4 C lime juice with water. Once the tequila cooked down a little I added in about 1.5 C of pico de gallo and 1/2 C cilatntro. I then added a little chili powder, salt and pepper. It came out delicious!

This was great! I used 1/4 cup tequila and 1/4 cup beer to 1 pound of shrimp and also added some red pepper flakes, sweet red and yellow peppers, onions and some spinach and diced tomato at the end of cooking it, as a filler. Put in flour tortilla and topped with black beans. I WILL be making this again!

sooo good...a favorite in our house...per other reviews I do 1/4 c. light beer, 1/4 c. taquila. I also add more cilantro, a little extra butter and juice of 2-4 limes depending on size I have and creole seasoning. We spoon mexican style rice, shrimp and sauce and chunks of avocado in small warmed flour tortillas. It is so good, a must try!
These shrimp were very tasty, however, we added lime juice to the tequila and would marinate the shrimp for at least a half-hour prior in the future to really give them a taste.

This was so easy to make! 

I took the advice of other reviewers and marinated the shrimp in tequila for about a half hour before cooking it. Therefore, I added less tequila than called for when cooking the shrimp and then I added lime zest for extra flavor.

Next time I plan to make this, I will add some jalapenos in with the garlic.
Came out delicious, easy to make, I would make it again 🥰🥰🥰

If you made this and didn’t like it you messed up or you are broken. Use good tequila, fresh limes and fresh cilantro. 1/2 a cup of light beer adds to it as well. Cuervo is tequila. Use Milagro or better.
Super easy, and delicious. I highly recommend making this recipe.
This was awesome. We made it as an appetizer, used 1 1/2 pounds of shrimp, and 1/4 cup of tequila. We would use a bit more garlic next time, but the taste was fantastic!
Really yummy! I did half tequila and half beer but that’s the only change. Will make it again and again!
We loved this recipe....I did cut down the amount of tequila....used 1/4 cup tequila and 1/4 cup beer.
It turned out quite delicious, combined with a rice recipe on here made a perfect dinner.
This is such an easy and delicious meal. I sure will make this again.
My college kids loved the shrimp. Had to substitute rum for tequila and it was a big hit.
